name: transgender medicine overview
title: Transgender medicine pathway: assess whether a young person has gender dysphoria, then climb the reversibility ladder from fully reversible puberty blockers at Tanner 2, to partially reversible masculinizing testosterone or feminizing estrogen with anti-androgen after the WPATH criteria are met, to irreversible surgery after mental health referral, each with its regimen, effects, risks and monitoring

nodes.title: Gender-affirming care: assess, then climb the REVERSIBILITY ladder
lines: puberty blockers FULLY reversible → gender-affirming hormones PARTIALLY reversible → surgery IRREVERSIBLE
guidelines: World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH) Standards of Care (SOC) v8, 2022 · Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline, 2017

nodes.title: Assess
lines: is it gender dysphoria?

nodes.title: FULLY reversible
lines: pauses puberty

nodes.title: PARTIALLY reversible: gender-affirming hormones
lines: two goals: 1 · SUPPRESS endogenous sex hormones and the secondary sex characteristics of the designated gender · 2 · REPLACE, as for a hypogonadal patient

nodes.title: IRREVERSIBLE
lines: the last step

nodes.title: Criteria for hormones
lines: ADULTS (WPATH): persistent, well-documented gender dysphoria · capacity for a fully informed decision and consent · age of majority · significant medical or mental health concerns reasonably well-CONTROLLED
after a psychosocial assessment + informed consent · referral from the mental health professional who assessed (unless the hormone provider is qualified to assess)
ADOLESCENTS: confirmed persistence of gender incongruence · able to consent · preferably parental consent/support · usually ~16 y, earlier if compelling reasons · decided by team, adolescent + family

nodes.title: Gender dysphoria
lines: DISCONTENT: body or assigned gender INCONGRUENT with gender identity
with social stigma, isolation, rejection

nodes.title: Puberty blockers
lines: hit the PAUSE button on puberty

nodes.title: Masculinizing: TESTOSTERONE
lines: transgender males · FTM (female-to-male)

nodes.title: Feminizing: ESTROGEN ± anti-androgen
lines: transgender females · MTF (male-to-female)

nodes.title: Surgery
lines: gender re-assignment surgery
IRREVERSIBLE

nodes.title: Features
lines: marked, persistent INCONGRUENCE: perceived gender vs assigned sex
desire to transition + be accepted in the experienced gender
strong DISLIKE of sexual anatomy or anticipated pubertal changes
desire for sex characteristics to match
children: make-believe, toys, activities, playmates of the experienced gender

nodes.title: Canada 2022
lines: 1 in 300 aged 15+ trans or non-binary
2/3 under 35

nodes.title: Adolescents
lines: 1.2–4.1% report a gender identity unlike assigned sex

nodes.title: Criteria
lines: long-lasting gender nonconformity or dysphoria
dysphoria WORSENED with the onset of puberty
co-existing psychological, medical or social problems addressed
informed consent

nodes.title: TANNER 2 reached
lines: no hormonal therapy until puberty has STARTED

nodes.title: Regimens
lines: enanthate or cypionate 100–200 mg intramuscular (IM) every 2 wk, or subcutaneous (SC) 50% weekly
undecanoate 1000 mg every 12 wk
gel 1.6% 50–100 mg/d · patch 2.5–7.5 mg/d

nodes.title: Injection
lines: every 2–4 wk · fluctuating T (testosterone): "roller coaster"

nodes.title: Transdermal
lines: daily · patch irritation · contamination · sweating

nodes.title: Oral: 2–3× daily
lines: needs fatty food · level CANNOT be monitored

nodes.title: Estradiol
lines: oral 2–6 mg/d
patch 0.025–0.2 mg/d, new patch every 3–5 d
valerate or cypionate IM 5–30 mg every 2 wk, or 2–10 mg weekly

nodes.title: Anti-androgen
lines: spirono-lactone 100–300 mg/d · cyproterone acetate 25–50 mg/d

nodes.title: GnRH agonist
lines: 3.75 mg SC monthly or 11.25 mg SC 3-monthly

nodes.title: 1 · Referral (WPATH)
lines: 1 or 2 (by surgery type) from a qualified mental health professional
documents history, progress + eligibility
ONTARIO: TWO health care providers must support it

nodes.title: 2 · GENITAL surgery not until
lines: legal age of MAJORITY + ≥ 1 year living continuously in the intended gender role

nodes.title: TOP surgery can be earlier
lines: age 16 · hormones × 1 year · patience
~preferably after ample time in the role

nodes.title: 1 · Gender identity
lines: "born in the wrong body? ever felt like that?"

nodes.title: 2 · Persistence
lines: "how long have you felt a girl/boy?" · "how did puberty affect you?"

nodes.title: 3 · Gender non- conforming behaviour
lines: toys · underwear · swimwear · fantasy characters

nodes.title: 4 · Source of distress
lines: "what thoughts make you sad?" · "what do you think about your body?"

nodes.title: Buys time
lines: to assess PERSISTENCE of the affirmed gender as the child matures, before the physical changes of puberty
improved behaviour, emotional + depressive symptoms
~GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) agonist, e.g. leuprolide †

nodes.title: Slows growth
lines: puberty · linear growth · androgen- dependent hair · voice deepening

nodes.title: Lessens changes
lines: breast or testicular/ penile growth · periods · libido · "teenage behaviour"

nodes.title: Onset 1–6 months
lines: skin oiliness/acne · fat redistribution · periods STOP · clitoral enlargement · vaginal atrophy

nodes.title: Onset 6–12 months
lines: facial/body hair (max 4–5 y) · scalp hair loss · muscle mass/strength (max 2–5 y) · voice DEEPENS (max 1–2 y)

nodes.title: PERMANENT
lines: hair growth · height ↑ · bone mineral content (BMC) ↑ · deeper voice · clitoris enlarged, vaginal dryness · male-pattern balding

nodes.title: NOT permanent
lines: muscle mass ↑ · libido ↑ · no periods · acne
UNKNOWN: fertility; uterus, cervix, breasts, ovaries

nodes.title: Onset 1–3 months
lines: ↓ sexual desire · ↓ spontaneous erections (max 3–6 mo)

nodes.title: Onset 3–6 months
lines: fat redistribution · ↓ muscle · softer, less oily skin · BREAST growth · ↓ testicular volume (max 2–3 y)

nodes.title: Slow or none
lines: terminal hair ↓ at 6–12 mo (max > 3 y) · scalp hair variable · VOICE: no change

nodes.title: PERMANENT
lines: breast development · BMC ↑

nodes.title: NOT permanent
lines: softer skin · less muscle · female fat pattern · less body hair · slower balding

nodes.title: After hormone transition
lines: transgender males: ovariectomy can be considered
mastectomy done: yearly sub- + periareolar breast exams · not done: mammograms (American Cancer Society)

nodes.title: Mental health outcomes
lines: with hormones + a multidisciplinary team: like the general population

nodes.title: SUICIDALITY 2–3× more frequent
lines: Ontario trans youth: 47% thought about suicide, 19% attempted

nodes.title: FAMILY SUPPORT
lines: suicide risk 4% if supportive vs 60% if non-supportive

nodes.title: Multidisciplinary care
lines: youth treated with hormones, surgery + a team with mental health clinicians: outcomes like the general population

nodes.title: FERTILITY: discuss BEFORE hormones
lines: reproductive options first (WPATH)

nodes.title: Oocyte preservation
lines: EXPENSIVE: no Ministry of Health (MOH) plan covers it
may be traumatizing
must be OFF hormones with 1–2 normal periods

nodes.title: Likely ↑ risk (WPATH)
lines: POLYCYTHEMIA · weight gain · acne · androgenic alopecia (balding) · SLEEP APNEA

nodes.title: Possible ↑ risk
lines: liver enzymes ↑ · HYPERLIPIDEMIA
with risk factors (e.g. age): psychiatric destabilization at high T · cardiovascular disease (CVD) · hypertension · type 2 diabetes

nodes.title: MONITOR (Endocrine Society)
lines: review every 3 mo in year 1, then 1–2×/yr

T every 3 mo until normal male range: 400–700 ng/dL MIDWAY between enanthate/cypionate injections · undecanoate: just before the next dose (< 400 → shorten interval) · gel: after ≥ 1 wk, ≥ 2 h after applying
hematocrit or hemoglobin: baseline, every 3 mo in year 1, then 1–2×/yr · weight, blood pressure (BP), lipids

nodes.title: Total T + SHBG
lines: sex hormone-binding globulin falls in OBESITY · free androgen index = T / SHBG

nodes.title: Screening
lines: bone if T stopped or not taken · cervix if present · breasts

nodes.title: VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM
lines: likely ↑ · greater with ORAL than transdermal estrogen

nodes.title: Likely ↑ risk (WPATH)
lines: gallstones · liver enzymes ↑ · weight gain · HYPERTRIGLYCERIDEMIA · CVD with risk factors

nodes.title: Possible ↑ risk
lines: hypertension · hyperprolactinemia or PROLACTINOMA · type 2 diabetes with risk factors

nodes.title: MONITOR (Endocrine Society)
lines: review every 3 mo in year 1, then 1–2×/yr
T + estradiol every 3 mo: T < 50 ng/dL · estradiol ≤ peak physiologic 100–200 pg/mL
SPIRONOLACTONE: potassium every 3 mo in year 1, then yearly

nodes.title: Breast cancer
lines: Stein: risk ↑ · WPATH: no ↑ or inconclusive

nodes.title: Screening
lines: cancer as usual, for tissues present · bone density

nodes.title: SHARED responsibility
lines: mental health professionals who recommend surgery share ETHICAL + LEGAL responsibility with the surgeon

panels.title: Before starting hormones (WPATH)
items: 1 · evaluate: physical transition goals, health history, exam, risk assessment, relevant labs
2 · discuss expected + adverse effects, incl. ↓ FERTILITY: reproductive options BEFORE starting
3 · confirm capacity to understand risks + benefits
4 · ongoing monitoring: exam + labs for effect and side effects
5 · communicate with primary care, mental health, surgeon
6 · if needed, a brief written statement of medical supervision

panels.title: Role of the endocrinologist
items: cannot see all patients over the long term

panels.title: Four terms
items: SEX: biological (chromosomes, gonads, genitalia) · male, female, DSD (difference of sex development)
GENDER IDENTITY: the person's own articulation · cis-gender, trans-gender, gender non-conforming
SEXUAL ORIENTATION: the sex of those one is attracted to

panels.title: Bone + cancer screening (Endocrine Society)
items: transgender females: bone mineral density (BMD) at baseline; low risk: osteoporosis screen at 60, or if not taking hormones
transgender males: osteoporosis screen if T stopped, not taken, or bone-loss risks · cervix per American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
